study type: Retrospective review of maternal death audits
exposure: Types of delays in care (seeking, reaching, receiving)
outcome: Specific causes of maternal death (e.g., obstetric hemorrhage, hypertensive disorder, infection)
cohort: The study analyzed 191 maternal death audits for refugee women who died between 2017 and 2019 in 43 refugee camps across eight countries in the East and Horn of Africa.
finding: Obstetric hemorrhage was the leading direct cause of maternal death (49%), and delays in receiving care were highly prevalent (81% of cases with identified delays), highlighting significant capacity gaps in emergency obstetric care.
country: Multiple countries in the East and Horn of Africa (region)
